rules.name: Basel 3.1 Output Floor — Capital Adequacy for Commercial Lending
rules.source_legislation: PRA PS17/23 (Basel 3.1 UK transposition); Capital Requirements Regulation (CRR) UK; Capital Requirements Directive (CRD V) UK
rules.description: The bank's risk-weighted assets (RWAs) calculated using internal models (IRB) must not fall below a floor of a specified percentage of the Standardised Approach RWA equivalent. The output floor phases in annually from 50% (2025) to 72.5% (2030). This directly increases capital requirements for IRB banks with large commercial lending books, particularly those with commercial real estate exposures. Capital plans, ICAAP, and commercial credit strategy must be updated to reflect the rising floor at each phase-in step.
disclosure_obligations: Pillar 3 disclosure of RWA and capital ratios updated at least annually (quarterly for large banks)
ICAAP submitted to PRA biennially or upon material change, incorporating output floor projections
COREP capital templates filed with PRA quarterly, reflecting output floor constraint where binding
constraints: IRB models for commercial exposures require PRA approval and annual validation
Commercial real estate risk weights under revised SA increase materially — underwriting standards must reflect higher capital cost
Lending strategy must be reviewed against capital budget at each output floor phase-in step

rules.name: Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023 — Digital Trade Document Acceptance
rules.source_legislation: Electronic Trade Documents Act 2023 (ETDA), in force September 2023; UK MLETR alignment
rules.description: The bank may now accept and issue electronic bills of lading, bills of exchange, promissory notes, and warehouse receipts that have the same legal standing as paper equivalents, provided the electronic document system meets the ETDA reliability criteria (uniqueness, control, integrity). The bank's trade finance operations must update documentation acceptance policies to recognise ETDA-compliant electronic trade documents and update credit facilities and guarantee issuance procedures accordingly.
disclosure_obligations: Updated standard trade finance facility terms noting ETDA-compliant electronic document acceptance
Client-facing communications confirming digital trade document eligibility under ETDA
Legal opinion on compliance of each electronic document platform with ETDA reliability criteria
constraints: Electronic trade documents are only legally equivalent to paper if the platform meets all ETDA reliability criteria
Bank must maintain an audit trail demonstrating exclusive control of electronic bills of lading and similar negotiable instruments
Cross-border trade documents involving non-UK jurisdictions may still require paper originals depending on foreign law

rules.name: Business Banking Resolution Service (BBRS) — SME Dispute Handling
rules.source_legislation: Business Banking Resolution Service (BBRS) participation agreement; FCA Business Plan 2024/25
rules.description: The bank must participate in BBRS as a dispute resolution scheme for eligible SME customers (up to £10m annual turnover) whose complaints relate to historical or current business banking products and services. Eligible businesses that cannot resolve complaints directly with the bank may refer them to BBRS free of charge. The bank must fund BBRS participation fees and implement all BBRS determinations.
disclosure_obligations: BBRS availability disclosed in all SME complaint-handling communications
BBRS leaflet provided to eligible SME customers at account opening and upon complaint acknowledgement
Annual report to BBRS on complaints referred, resolved, and upheld rates
constraints: BBRS covers SME customers with up to £10m annual turnover
Bank must implement BBRS final determinations within the specified timeframe (typically 28 days)
BBRS complaints must be acknowledged within 5 working days and resolved within 8 weeks before BBRS referral becomes available

rules.name: PRA Third-Party Risk Management — Material Outsourcing in Commercial Banking
rules.source_legislation: PRA SS2/21 (Outsourcing and Third-Party Risk); Financial Services and Markets Act 2023 Part 5 (UK DORA-equivalent); PRA CP30/23
rules.description: The bank must maintain a register of material outsourcing and third-party arrangements within the commercial banking capability — covering trade finance platforms (Finastra, Surecomp), treasury technology (Kyriba, FIS), and any cloud infrastructure providers. Material arrangements require board-approved exit plans, concentration risk assessment, and PRA notification. Third-party ICT incidents that affect important business services must be reported to PRA within prescribed timescales.
disclosure_obligations: Material outsourcing register filed with PRA and updated annually
Operational resilience self-assessment including third-party dependencies submitted to PRA
Material ICT incident report to PRA and FCA within 4 hours (initial) and 24 hours (intermediate)
constraints: Cannot outsource accountability for commercial banking important business services — Senior Manager accountability must remain in-house
Material outsourcing contracts must include exit termination rights and access-for-audit provisions
Concentration risk must be assessed where two or more material business services depend on the same third-party provider
PRA must be notified before entering into new material outsourcing arrangements above threshold

rules.name: FCA SME Lending Rules — Affordability and Disclosure
rules.source_legislation: FCA FS23/3 (SME Lending Review); FCA consultation paper (expected final rules 2025–2026)
rules.description: Following the FCA's SME lending review, final rules are expected requiring standardised APR-equivalent disclosure for business term loans, affordability stress-testing for facilities above £25,000, cooling-off periods for unsolicited credit increases, and fair value assessments for SME lending products. The bank must update its SME credit origination, documentation, and pricing processes in advance of the rule commencement date.
disclosure_obligations: Standardised cost of credit disclosure (APRC-equivalent) in business loan offer letters
Affordability stress-test summary provided to borrower for facilities above £25,000
Cooling-off period and right-to-cancel terms included in credit increase communications
constraints: Unsolicited credit limit increases must include a minimum 14-day opt-in cooling-off period
Affordability stress-testing must use PRA-aligned interest rate shock scenarios
Products found to deliver poor value under Consumer Duty-equivalent SME assessment must be remediated

rules.name: Business Current Account Portability — CASS Reform for SMEs
rules.source_legislation: HM Treasury and FCA CASS consultation for business accounts (expected 2025); Payment and Settlement Systems Act 2023
rules.description: HM Treasury and the FCA are expected to mandate 7-day switching for business current accounts equivalent to the personal account CASS regime. The bank must build operational capability to originate and receive CASS business switches within 7 calendar days, including transfer of standing orders, direct debit mandates, and balance. This is a major strategic risk that reduces the structural switching friction protecting incumbent commercial banks.
disclosure_obligations: CASS business switching guarantee displayed on all business account opening documentation
Switch tracking confirmation communicated to SME customer throughout the 7-day process
Switching statistics reported to Pay.UK and FCA per scheme rules
constraints: 7-day switching window applies from initiation to completion including transfer of all payment mandates
Bank must redirect all misdirected payments for 36 months after a switch
Cannot impose contractual barriers or fees that would discourage switching
